title: Iterated cones impose affine support
statement: Let X=\operatorname{Spec}(A) be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let g_1,\dots,g_s\in A, put T=V(g_1,\dots,g_s), and let E be a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex]. Put C_0=E and, for 1\le i\le s, let C_i be a cone of multiplication by g_i on C_{i-1}. Then C_s is perfect and its cohomology sheaves vanish on X\setminus T. If moreover U\subset X is a quasi-compact open, F is a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_U) with E|_U\cong F\oplus F[1], and multiplication by each g_i is zero on F, then C_s|_U\cong\bigoplus_{j=0}^{s+1}F[j]^{\oplus\binom{s+1}{j}}.

proof.text: Induct over Fin (s+1). The initial object is perfect by hE. At the successor apply the first clause of isPerfect_two_out_of_three to the scalar distinguished triangle and use the induction hypothesis for both copies of its input.

Induct over k with the invariant: at every x belonging to some D(g_i) with i.val < k.val, every cohomology stalk of C_k is subsingleton. At k=0 the inequality is impossible. At the successor, if i=k use the unit branch of scalar_cone_stalk_vanishing. Otherwise i<k and the induction hypothesis supplies its acyclic-input branch. At k=Fin.last s every i in Fin s meets the inequality.

Write R for the specified derived restriction. Inductively identify R(C_k) with the binomial sum B_(k.val+1)(F). The initial isomorphism is the supplied R(C_0) isomorphic to F plus F[1], followed by the initial clause of binomial_shift_biproduct. For a successor use restricted_scalar_cone_split with the finite binomial index type and shift function p mapped to p.1.val. Map the induction isomorphism across the binary biproduct and its shift, then compose with the Pascal clause of binomial_shift_biproduct. At Fin.last s this is the required formula.
